name: Token auction

subjectOf.text: If underwriters decline to reclaim their encumbered tokens, that breach is resolved by selling the encumbered tokens, plus additional freshly minted tokens as needed, in an auction open to current DAO participants and to outsiders wishing to join.
subjectOf.abstract: In such a case, the encumbered tokens, along with additional freshly minted tokens as needed, would be sold in an auction. All current DAO participants as well as outsiders interested in joining the DAO may bid for the tokens in this auction.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Decentralized Underwriting (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396542
scope_conditions: breach by underwriters on a specific policy

subjectOf.text: Even where the underwriters of a policy breach the contract, the auction of the encumbered tokens together with the sale of additional tokens as needed ensures the policy holder's claim is fully met.
subjectOf.abstract: Even if the underwriters of a particular policy were to breach the contract, the auction of the encumbered tokens and the sale of additional tokens as needed ensures that the policy holder's claim is fully met.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Decentralized Underwriting (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396542

subjectOf.text: The proposed DAO design is likely to lower barriers to entry in insurance, since non traditional firms and even individual investors can buy tokens at auction and then either underwrite with them or hold them passively.
subjectOf.abstract: In addition, the particular design outlined above is likely to facilitate the entry of new players to the insurance market. It is possible for a DAO to allow the participation of non-traditional firms and even individual investors.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Decentralized Underwriting (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396542
